notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. The chapters are a reading order built from the ayat, not a chronology the Quran claims; surah order is not time order. The glad tidings are told in Zakariyya's account too; this draft states only what concerns Yahya. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The angels called to Zakariyya while he stood praying in the mihrab that God gives him good news of Yahya, confirming a word from God, a leader, one who holds back, and a prophet from among the righteous.
God told Zakariyya of a boy whose name is Yahya, for whom He had not made a namesake before.

chapters.summary_md: Zakariyya was given good news of Yahya, a boy with that name for whom God had made no namesake before, a leader and a prophet from among the righteous [c1][c2].
chapters.body_md: The angels called to Zakariyya while he stood praying in the mihrab that God gives him good news of Yahya, confirming a word from God, a leader, one who holds back, and a prophet from among the righteous [c1]. God told Zakariyya of a boy whose name is Yahya, for whom He had not made a namesake before [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The good news in 3:39 describes Yahya in a series of ways: as confirming a word from God, a leader, one who holds back, and a prophet from among the righteous [c1]. The good news in 19:7 gives his name and says that the name had no namesake before [c2]. The ayat do not say whether this is the same moment [c1][c2].
chapters.kids_md: Zakariyya was told that he would have a boy named Yahya [c1][c2]. Yahya would be a leader and a prophet from among the righteous [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The good news gives the name first and the qualities after it [c1][c2]. A reader may notice that being a prophet is joined with being from among the righteous [c1].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: the sense of the Arabic hasur, one who holds back, or of sayyid, a leader; the ayah gives the words and the reviewer decides the wording.
- Not established: what the word from God is; the ayah says only that Yahya confirms it.
- Not established: the sense of the word for namesake, which can also read as equal; the reviewer decides the wording.
- Not established: Yahya's birth, parents' ages or the place of his birth beyond what the ayat of Zakariyya's account say.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: an identification of the word from God with a person; it is not used in the story texts.

claims.statement_en: Yahya was told to take the Book with strength, and God gave him judgment as a child.
God gave him tenderness from Himself, and purity, and he was one who feared God.
He was dutiful to his parents, and was not a tyrant or disobedient.
Peace is on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive.

chapters.summary_md: Yahya was told to take the Book with strength; God gave him judgment, tenderness and purity, he feared God and was dutiful to his parents, and peace is on him [c1][c2][c3][c4].
chapters.body_md: Yahya was told to take the Book with strength, and God gave him judgment as a child [c1]. God gave him tenderness from Himself, and purity, and he was one who feared God [c2]. He was dutiful to his parents, and was not a tyrant or disobedient [c3]. Peace is on him the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive [c4].
chapters.deep_md: The first words are a command addressed to him by name [c1]. The following ayat describe him as a description, by what God gave him and by what he was [c2][c3]. The last ayah is a statement of peace on the day of his birth, the day of his death and the day he is raised [c4]. The words tenderness (hanan) and purity (zakah) are given without further explanation [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Yahya was told to hold on firmly to the Book [c1]. He was kind to his parents and was not harsh [c3]. Peace is on him [c4].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): The description joins duty to God with duty to parents [c2][c3]. A reader may notice that the ayat on Yahya end with peace upon him on the day he was born, the day he dies and the day he is raised alive [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: which Book Yahya was told to take, or what it contained; the ayah says only the Book.
- Not established: what judgment as a child consisted of, or how old he was; the ayah says child and no more.
- Not established: the exact senses of hanan (tenderness) and zakah (purity) here; the reviewer decides the wording.
- Not established: how he died, or when; the ayah says only the day he dies.
- Not established: whether the peace on him is a greeting or a statement; the ayah has the word alone.

chapters.title_en: Given, and named among the righteous

claims.statement_en: God answered Zakariyya, gave him Yahya, and put his wife right for him.
The ayah says of them that they used to hasten to good deeds, call on God in hope and in fear, and were humble before Him.
Yahya is named, with Zakariyya and others, each described as being among the righteous.

chapters.summary_md: God gave Yahya to Zakariyya in answer to his call, and Yahya is named among those each described as righteous [c1][c3].
chapters.body_md: God answered Zakariyya, gave him Yahya, and put his wife right for him [c1]. The ayah says of them that they used to hasten to good deeds, call on God in hope and in fear, and were humble before Him [c2]. Yahya is named, with Zakariyya and others, each described as being among the righteous [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah on the gift of Yahya is brief and speaks of the answer to Zakariyya's call [c1]. The description that follows is in the plural and does not say who is included [c2]. In 6:85 Yahya is named in a list, and each in the list is described as righteous [c3].
chapters.kids_md: God answered Zakariyya and gave him Yahya [c1]. Yahya is named among the righteous [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): Yahya is spoken of first as a gift from God and then as one of the righteous [c1][c3]. The ayah describes those it speaks of as hastening to good deeds and humble before God [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who they are in 21:90, whether Zakariyya, his wife and Yahya or others; the plural is not explained.
- Not established: what put his wife right means, or whether it refers to her barrenness.
- Not established: why the others named in 6:85 are listed with Yahya; this draft states only the part that concerns Yahya and Zakariyya.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, on Yahya and his death. None is used in this draft.
The words hasur (3:39), sayyid, hanan and zakah (19:13), the sense of the word for namesake (19:7), and judgment as a child (19:12) are left open; a scholar should decide how the page words each.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of the word from God in 3:39 with a person, and accounts of Yahya's life and death. None is used in the story texts.
The Quran gives the glad tidings of Yahya, his description, and the peace upon him; it does not give a story of his life, so the chapters are short.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.
